title.narrative: Enhanced skills, employability and entrepreneurial capacity of target populations especially youth, women and persons with disabilities

description.narrative: Malawi’s relatively high unemployment rates which is also considered as untapped human capital which if fully engaged would contribute to the socio-economic development of the country. The youth who complete secondary education and do not proceed to higher education remain unemployed due to lack of necessary skills for the job market as well as entrepreneurship. This skills gap needs to be addressed if Malawi is to harness the idle labour force for meaningful development. To do so, the education system needs to be reformed to include entrepreneurship, and vocational skills development to improve employability as well as entrepreneurship of the young Malawians thereby reducing youth unemployment. To implement R208 on quality apprenticeship programme Structured apprenticeship programmes are increasingly recognized as key policy tools to facilitate the transitions of young people from school to employment. Quality apprenticeships offer young people direct work experience, as well as applied knowledge and skills. This combination enables apprentices to understand the logic behind the job they are tasked with, cope with unpredictable situations, and acquire higher level/transferable skills. In addition, apprenticeship programmes give apprentices a chance to demonstrate their productivity potential to employers who may otherwise be reluctant to hire fresh graduates. For all these reasons, they can be a key strategy to improve young people’s access to decent job opportunities however faces the challenges of the industries to absorb the number of young people into their workplaces due to limited resources or capacity to handle such numbers. Partners of this intervention include Government of Malawi through the Technical, Entrepreneurial and Vocational Education and Training (TEVET) Authority, Ministry of Labour, the Norwegian Government (NORAD), the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), Rural Youth, Communities, and other United Nations agencies.
